title: Your Attention Is the Bottleneck, Not Your Agents — Zack Proser, WorkOS
talk_summary: A WorkOS engineer argues that human attention, not agent capacity, is now the bottleneck, and shares personal workflow tricks: giving agents Slack/Linear access to self-verify loops, voice-first prompting, remote-controlling sessions from a phone, and mining saved session logs for recurring friction.

takeaways.technique: Self-verification loop with external tool access
takeaways.what_they_do: Gives the agent read/write access to the real system (Slack channel, Linear) and instructs it to fix the bug, exercise the actual product path, and verify the outcome before declaring done, looping until verified.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You need to fix this and then you also need to verify your own work and don't stop until you've done that.

takeaways.technique: Mine session logs for recurring friction
takeaways.what_they_do: Scheduled pass over saved agent conversation logs (JSONL) to find where lots of thinking tokens or back-and-forth were spent, then turn those into new skills/tools so the loop tightens next week.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Look for the patterns where you had to do a significant amount of spending thinking tokens to get something right

takeaways.technique: Agent-ready ticket queue with polling loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Tags tickets as 'agent ready' and runs a loop every 15 minutes, day and night, that pulls and works them, instead of ad-hoc dispatch.
takeaways.evidence_quote: marking tickets with a tag says agent ready and then having a loop that's literally going every 15 minutes all day long

takeaways.what_they_do: For large multi-part features, gives each parallel agent its own worktree so they don't step on each other, paired with clearly scoped prompts and stronger verification gates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: get work trees first of all so that the agents can run in truly in parallel without stepping on each other's work

takeaways.what_they_do: Defines escalating gates: (1) lint/build/unit tests via hooks on every change, (2) agent drives a browser to click through critical flows like login, (3) a separate agent checks work against a written constitution and gives feedback.
takeaways.evidence_quote: gate two is when you tell the Claude code that you must verify your own work with the browser, click through it

takeaways.technique: Give agents the highest-cost context-switch tool
takeaways.what_they_do: Connects the agent to the system that causes the most human context switching (Slack, Linear) so it can triage mentions/DMs, dedupe asks, and surface real tickets without a human combing through.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it can see are there at mentions, are there DMs, are there actually like high priority asks that need to be actioned
